name: clear_global_word_return
description: Writes zero to one global word and then returns the value it was handed, so the caller's result is unchanged.

name: resolve_table_entry_pointer
description: Repeatedly fetches an index from a routine and stores the matching table address in the per-entry record, retrying until a counter reaches its limit. On success it records a result word and clears the pending flags; on failure it resets the state and stores an error code.

name: set_flag_from_test_result
description: Calls a routine and stores 1 in a global flag when it returns zero, otherwise stores minus one.

name: store_indexed_pointer_first
description: Looks up a table entry using the value a routine returns and saves the resulting address, offset from the record base, in the record's first pointer field.

name: load_indexed_word_to_global
description: Calls a routine and copies the 16-bit table word selected by its result into a global word.

name: store_indexed_pointer_second
description: Looks up a table entry using the value a routine returns and saves the resulting address, offset from the record base, in the record's second pointer field.

name: chain_two_calls_return_pair
description: Calls two subroutines in sequence and returns whatever the two result registers hold afterwards as one 64-bit value, without any decision of its own.

name: start_audio_channel_playback
description: If the record's active flag is clear, it waits while the audio channel is still busy, loads the sample pointer and length into that channel's registers, marks the channel as playing, and enables its DMA and interrupt bits in the custom chip control registers.

name: copy_block_then_call_handler
description: Copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed table in the record into a caller-supplied buffer when one is given, then calls a handler stored in the record through a function pointer.

name: build_record_with_handler
description: Walks a list to find the largest size stored in its entries, allocates a record of that size, fills it with a repeating tag pattern, copies a 16-word state block into it, stores a handler pointer, and returns zero on success or minus one if an allocation fails.

name: copy_block_then_call_handler
description: Copies sixteen 32-bit words from a fixed table in the record into a caller-supplied buffer when one is given, then calls a handler stored in the record through a function pointer.

name: parse_arguments_and_launch
description: Entry routine that allocates a process record, splits the command-line string into null-terminated arguments (honouring quoted text and the star escapes for newline and escape), runs the tool, then closes the libraries and frees the record.

name: store_result_and_run_cleanups
description: Stores its argument in a slot of the current process record, runs up to three cleanup routines chosen by which record fields are non-zero, and returns the stored argument.

name: launch_workbench_tool
description: Applies an XOR loop to a global string (twice with the same key, which leaves the text unchanged), allocates a buffer, looks up Workbench and icon library routines, sets up the argument and icon structures, and reports an error if the tool cannot be started.

name: compare_null_terminated_strings
description: Compares two null-terminated strings byte by byte and returns minus one, zero or one according to whether the first is less than, equal to or greater than the second.

name: build_linked_node_list
description: Walks a linked table, allocating a zeroed eight-byte node per entry, filling its second word from a library lookup, chaining the nodes together, and returning the first node (or nothing if an allocation fails).

name: pad_release_version_string
description: Checks whether the character at offset twenty of the buffer is '2' and whether the buffer's leading text matches the global reference text; if both hold, it writes a dot and four spaces at offset seventeen.

name: write_dot_padding_field
description: Writes a dot and four spaces into the five bytes starting at offset seventeen of the buffer.

name: skip_matching_reference_text
description: Advances through the buffer while it matches the global reference text character by character, stopping at the first mismatch or when the reference text ends.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so calling it performs no work.

name: forward_with_stack_slot
description: Forwards its two arguments to another routine together with the address of a fixed stack slot, then returns nothing.

name: format_message_and_output
description: Runs the exec formatting routine into a 140-byte stack buffer, measures the resulting text, and passes the buffer and its length to an output routine when the text is not empty.

name: run_port_request_loop
description: Sets up a port control block, then loops reading request codes from a queue and dispatching each one: read and write commands, two pending-event codes that set flags, and a completion code that clears pending state. The loop ends once no request is outstanding.

name: validate_disk_allocation_bitmap
description: Writes the current count into a text line, then compares each bit of the disk bitmap against the expected block map, counting discrepancies and walking the block chains; it finishes by reporting the summary.

name: copy_memory_then_jump
description: Copies memory through the exec library, then transfers control through a jump target the decompiler could not recover, so the rest of the handler's work happens elsewhere.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Contains no valid code, only decoder warnings for bad instruction data, so calling it does nothing useful.

name: allocate_serial_buffers
description: Frees any previously allocated serial buffer, allocates a new one of the requested size through exec memory allocation, records the pointer and size, clears two fields, and stores half and quarter size values as buffer thresholds.

name: set_request_status_byte
description: Writes a fixed status byte into the request and, when none of the masked status bits are set, calls a device library routine through the device base.

name: toggle_serial_interrupts_around_call
description: Disables the serial transmit and receive interrupts through the interrupt enable register, runs a routine while they are off, then re-enables both.

name: unlink_serial_request_from_queue
description: Clears the request's flag byte, then removes it from the active or pending queue according to its type, relinking its neighbours and adjusting the queue count; for two request types it also clears a pending-transmit bit, and it calls a library routine when the completion flag is clear.

name: finish_serial_request_unlink
description: Removes the request from the device's active slot or its queue, sets its status to the completion value, clears the request's busy bit, and calls a device library routine when its completion flag is clear.

name: remove_queued_serial_request
description: When the request is marked as queued, unlinks it from its list, decrements the queue count, sets its status and busy bits, and notifies the owner if it is not already complete.

name: complete_active_serial_request
description: Completes the active serial request: if it is the one currently running, it clears a break-state bit in the hardware control register and resets the active slot, then sets the request's status and notifies its owner.

name: unlink_and_signal_request
description: Unlinks a queued serial request from its list, decrements the queue count, marks it not busy and sets its status, then calls a device library routine to signal it if it is not already complete.

name: release_serial_request_node
description: If a pending counter is non-zero, marks the request as waiting and returns zero; otherwise it calls library routines to release the request's resources, unlinks its node from the list, and returns the stored status.

name: release_request_and_return_status
description: Calls several device library routines to release the request's resources, unlinks the request node from its list, and returns the status word saved in the request.

name: queue_serial_request_for_transfer
description: If the request has a non-zero size, it sets its queued flag and adds it to the pending list, then calls a device library routine; otherwise it calls a library routine to notify the owner when its completion flag is clear.

name: drain_serial_ring_buffer
description: Starts the next queued request, then copies bytes out of the receive ring buffer into its data area, wrapping at the buffer end. It stores an error status when the buffer is empty or a parity or overrun condition is flagged, and when the request is complete it unlinks it and notifies its owner.

name: fill_request_from_ring_buffer
description: Copies bytes from the serial ring buffer into the active request, wrapping at the buffer end, and stops at a terminator byte or when the buffer runs out. When the request completes it sets the completion status and dequeues the next pending request.

name: copy_ring_bytes_until_terminator
description: Stores each ring-buffer byte into the request's data area until the request's terminator byte appears or its count is reached, then completes the request and starts the next queued one.

name: drain_serial_ring_buffer_result
description: Copies buffered bytes into queued requests, starting the next request as each one finishes, and returns the final status value once no request is left in the queue.

name: clear_bit_and_drain_buffer
description: Clears a selected bit in the working value, then copies buffered bytes into queued requests as each finishes, and returns the working value once the queue is empty.

name: stub_return_only
description: Contains only a return instruction, so calling it performs no work.

name: set_status_and_drain_queue
description: Sets the request's status code to one of four fixed values based on the device flags, then copies buffered bytes into queued requests until the queue is empty or the active request completes.

name: set_serial_status_then_drain
description: Sets the request's status code from the device flags, then copies buffered bytes into queued requests and starts the next request whenever one completes.

name: set_error_status_then_drain
description: Sets a parity or overrun style status code on the request depending on the device error flags, then completes the request and drains the next queued requests from the ring buffer.

name: handle_serial_receive_interrupt
description: Serial receive interrupt handler: it reads the received data word and status, handles start and stop characters and flow-control state, stores ordinary bytes in the receive buffer, and then calls a device library routine.

name: store_byte_special_check
description: Compares the incoming byte with the device's special character; on a match it re-enables the transmit interrupt when a pending flag is set, otherwise it stores the byte in the ring buffer. It then notifies the owner through a library routine.

name: store_byte_or_flag_overflow
description: Stores the incoming byte in the receive ring buffer when space remains, advancing the write position and count; when the buffer is full it marks the overflow and calls a device library routine.

name: store_byte_unless_error
description: Stores the incoming byte in the ring buffer unless its error bit is set; when the error bit is set it marks the receive as failed and calls a device library routine.

name: store_byte_with_status_mask
description: Checks the incoming byte against the device's status mask and, when it matches, stores it in the ring buffer; otherwise it marks the receive as failed and calls a device library routine.

name: mark_receive_error_and_notify
description: Sets the receive error flag in the device state, records the current buffer position if none is stored, and calls a device library routine to notify the owner.

name: store_byte_and_notify
description: Stores the given byte in the receive ring buffer, advancing the write pointer and count, and then calls a device library routine to notify the owner.

name: set_pointer_and_notify
description: If the buffer position slot is empty, records the current buffer position there, then calls a routine and a device library routine to notify the owner.

name: reset_serial_control_state
description: Copies a saved byte into the device state and clears a status flag. It clears a CIA port bit when a mask is set, then either enables the transmit-buffer-empty interrupt or zeroes the state byte, depending on a flag.

name: set_serial_control_state
description: Copies another saved byte into the device state and sets its status flag. It sets a CIA port bit when a mask is set, then either enables the transmit-buffer-empty interrupt or zeroes the state byte, depending on a flag.

name: clear_serial_status_byte
description: Zeroes one status byte in the device state.

name: arm_serial_timeout
description: Marks a timeout as running, resets its counter to a fixed starting value, and calls a timer library routine to start it; if the start reports a failure, it sets the request's error status.

name: check_idle_receive_timeout
description: Clears a pending-check bit, and when the check was armed and the receive data register shows no incoming data, it marks a timeout and calls a device library routine to notify the owner.

name: filter_and_store_serial_byte
description: Masks the received data word, treats a match with the device's special character as a flow-control event that sets or clears the pending flag, and otherwise stores the byte in the ring buffer and notifies the owner through a library routine.

name: mark_transfer_ready_and_notify
description: Sets the transfer-ready flag, records the current buffer position if none is stored, and calls a device library routine to notify the owner.

name: schedule_serial_request
description: Zeroes the request's counter, then makes it the active request when the port is free, or appends it to the waiting list when it is not. When neither applies and its completion flag is clear, it calls a library routine to notify the owner.

name: activate_serial_request_slot
description: Stores the request in the device's active slot, zeroes its transfer counter, and enables the transmit-buffer-empty interrupt. If the request was already queued, it instead notifies the owner when its completion flag is clear.

name: stub_return_only
description: Contains only a return instruction, so calling it performs no work.

name: set_status_on_control_bits
description: When two control-line bits in the CIA port value are both set, it writes status code 13 into the request's status byte; otherwise it leaves the request unchanged.

name: transmit_next_serial_byte
description: Sends the next byte from the transmit buffer to the serial data register when the transmitter is ready, sending pending control characters first. When a request finishes it moves on to the next queued request and notifies the owner once the queue is empty.

name: record_received_byte_and_count
description: Records the received byte in the receive buffer and advances the receive counter; when the byte matches a terminator or the count limit is reached, it completes the request and notifies the owner, otherwise it sets the pending-transfer status bit.

name: record_byte_if_below_limit
description: Compares the received count with the request's limit and, while below it, records the next received byte and updates the counters; it completes the request and notifies the owner when a terminator or the limit is reached.

name: record_byte_with_error_bit
description: Adds an error status bit to the received byte when a flag is clear, records the byte and updates the counters, then completes the request and notifies the owner once a terminator or the count limit is reached.

name: pop_next_pending_request
description: Pops the next waiting request from the pending list, makes it the active request, zeroes its counter, and starts it when it is of the special type. When nothing is waiting, it sets the device state word to one.

name: set_device_state_idle
description: Writes the value one to the device's state word and returns, marking the device idle.

name: send_pending_control_word
description: Clears the pending-control byte and writes it, combined with the saved control word, to the serial data register; when no request is active or waiting it writes the idle value.

name: reset_serial_device_defaults
description: Disables the serial interrupts, clears the active and queued request slots and device flags, loads default line parameters into the device state, and re-enables the serial interrupts.

name: finish_and_notify_request
description: Runs the request completion routine, then calls a device library routine to notify the owner when the request's completion flag is clear.

name: flag_and_notify_active_request
description: Sets the pending-transfer flag when a waiting request exists, runs the completion routine for the active request if there is one, and calls a device library routine to notify the owner when its completion flag is clear, returning that result.

name: clear_flag_and_notify_active
description: Clears the pending-transfer flag, runs the completion routine for the active request if there is one, enables the transmit-buffer-empty interrupt, and calls a device library routine to notify the owner when its completion flag is clear.

name: clear_flag_with_interrupts_off
description: Disables the serial interrupts, runs a routine to clear the request's flag, re-enables the interrupts, and calls a device library routine to notify the owner when its completion flag is clear.

name: drain_linked_flag_list
description: Removes each entry from a linked list in turn, calling a routine on every entry until the list is empty.

name: stub_return_only
description: Contains only a return instruction, so calling it performs no work.

name: capture_serial_status_snapshot
description: Captures the CIA port status bits and the device's control flags into the request, stores the current transfer count, clears the device's pending flags, and calls a device library routine to notify the owner when its completion flag is clear.

name: start_or_queue_serial_request
description: Queues the request when a queue entry is waiting or when a flag is set; otherwise it runs a routine, records the request as active, and sets a serial line control bit in the custom chip control register.

name: start_request_with_line_control
description: Runs a routine to prepare the request; if that succeeds it records the request as active and sets a serial line control bit, otherwise it notifies the owner through a library routine and clears the active slot.

name: notify_and_clear_active_request
description: Calls a device library routine to notify the owner, then clears the active request slot.

name: finish_break_and_enable_transmit
description: Clears a pending-break flag, and when a break was pending for an active request of the special type, clears the serial line control bit, marks the request, and notifies the owner; it then enables the transmit-buffer-empty interrupt.

name: start_timed_serial_wait
description: Clears a pending-wait flag, stores a supplied value and a fixed starting count in the timeout block, and calls a timer library routine to start the wait. It returns the library result with its low byte cleared.

name: update_serial_enable_state
description: Sets or clears the device's enable flag from the request. When the transmitter is idle and nothing is queued, it toggles the serial interrupts around a routine call; otherwise it marks the request as deferred and notifies the owner when the completion flag is clear.

name: clear_enable_toggle_when_idle
description: Clears the device's enable flag and, when the transmitter is idle and nothing is queued, toggles the serial interrupts around a routine call; otherwise it marks the request as deferred. It notifies the owner through a library routine when the completion flag is clear.

name: toggle_serial_interrupts_and_notify
description: Disables the serial transmit and receive interrupts, runs a routine, re-enables them, and calls a device library routine to notify the owner when the completion flag is clear.

name: validate_and_apply_serial_params
description: Checks the requested serial parameters, such as word length, stop-bit mode and bit rate, against their allowed ranges, copies them into the device state when they pass, and sets an error status when they do not.

name: compute_unit_bit_masks
description: Builds the bit mask for the requested serial unit, doubling it for a second stop-bit mode and shifting it further when a flag is set, then stores the mask and looks up two derived timing values through routine routines.

name: set_invalid_parameter_status
description: Writes error status code 5 into the request to signal that the requested parameter is not supported.

name: compute_serial_period_register
description: Divides a fixed clock constant by the requested bit rate, scaled down for large rates, and stores the result as the serial period value; in a special framing mode it also sets the parity-related bits.

name: set_serial_period_from_divisor
description: Divides a supplied value by a divisor to obtain the serial period, writes it to the serial period register, and marks the period as set; in a special framing mode it also sets the parity-related bits.

name: open_serial_unit_and_init
description: Allocates a serial unit structure through a library call, opens a resource the unit needs, sets up its queues and handler pointers through another routine, and returns one on success or zero if any step fails.

name: init_serial_queues_and_handlers
description: Sets up the serial unit's queue heads, buffer pointers and handler pointers, then disables the serial transmit and receive interrupts and returns one.

name: record_interrupt_context_pointers
description: Stores the caller's context pointers, a fixed value of sixteen, and the global data address into an interrupt structure so the handler can find its device state.

name: init_serial_request_block
description: Initialises a serial request block: it sets the queue and handler pointers, calls a library routine, disables the serial transmit and receive interrupts, and returns one.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Contains only a return of zero, so calling it has no effect beyond returning that value.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Contains no valid code, only decoder warnings for bad instruction data from the keymap file, so the decompiler stops at its first instruction.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Contains no valid code, only decoder warnings for bad instruction data from the sound file, so the decompiler stops at its first instruction.

name: stub_bad_instruction_data
description: Contains no valid code, only decoder warnings for bad instruction data from the sound file, so the decompiler stops at its first instruction.

name: increment_count_clear_flag
description: Increments the 16-bit user count stored in the library base and clears a status bit in the base.

name: decrement_count_maybe_expunge
description: Decrements the 16-bit user count in the library base and, when it reaches zero while a status bit is set, calls the library's removal routine and returns its result, otherwise returns zero.

name: free_library_node_if_idle
description: If the user count is zero, unlinks the library node from its list, frees its memory through the exec library, and returns the saved value. Otherwise it sets the pending-removal bit and returns zero.

name: mark_pending_removal
description: Sets the pending-removal status bit in the library base and returns zero.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Contains only a return of zero, so calling it has no effect beyond returning that value.

name: open_dos_library_or_alert
description: Records the library base and caller data, opens the DOS library through the exec library and saves the returned base on success; on failure it raises an exec alert.

name: copy_saved_library_pointers
description: Copies two saved 32-bit values from the library structure into the global pointer slots.

name: call_helper_and_return
description: Calls one library routine and returns, with no other work.

description: Calls one library routine and returns, with no other work.

name: call_helper_and_return
description: Calls one library routine and returns, with no other work.

name: store_argument_in_result_field
description: Calls a library routine through the library base to obtain a structure, then stores the second argument in one fixed field of that structure.

name: obtain_and_register_object
description: Calls another routine to obtain an object; when one is returned it passes it to a second routine, and if that step fails it calls a cleanup routine and returns zero. Otherwise it returns the object.

name: create_icon_record_from_buffer
description: Creates a record through another routine, copies a 44-byte block and several saved fields from a stack buffer into it, and links it onto its parent's list when one exists. If the second routine fails it releases the record and returns zero.

name: fill_icon_record_from_buffer
description: Copies a 44-byte block and several saved fields from a stack buffer into an icon record, then links the record onto its parent's list when one is set.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Contains only a return of zero, so calling it has no effect beyond returning that value.

name: pack_icon_record_for_write
description: Packs an icon record into a local buffer that starts with a fixed header tag and version one, copying its 44-byte block and saved fields, then passes the buffer to a writer routine.

name: load_icon_file_records
description: Opens and reads a .info icon file: it locates the file by name, checks the header tag and version, then allocates and loads the image data and the optional tool-type and default-tool records, returning the new record or zero on failure.

name: read_icon_image_sections
description: Reads the remaining sections of an icon file: it checks the header tag and version, then reads the two position fields and the optional image, tool-type and default-tool data, allocating and filling each buffer in turn.

name: read_icon_string_lists
description: Reads two 32-bit position values and then the optional pointer fields of the icon record, including a counted list of pointers that it fills one entry at a time. It returns one on success and zero when a read fails.

name: read_counted_pointer_list
description: Reads a counted list of 32-bit pointers entry by entry, reducing the remaining byte count by four each time, then reads one optional trailing field. It returns one when all reads succeed and zero otherwise.

name: call_then_return_zero
description: Calls one routine and then returns zero.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so calling it performs no work.

name: write_icon_file_records
description: Writes an icon record to a .info file: it allocates a 260-byte scratch block, writes the header and fixed fields, then writes the optional image, tool-type and default-tool sections, returning one on success and zero if any write fails.

name: write_icon_record_body
description: Writes the optional sections of an icon record to its .info file: the image, tool-type and default-tool data, each with its own length, returning one on success and zero if any write fails.

name: write_icon_string_lists
description: Writes the counted pointer list and the optional trailing fields of an icon record to the file, each with a length prefix, then stores the updated write position in the record.

name: write_length_prefixed_string
description: Measures a null-terminated text string and writes its length, then writes each entry of the record's pointer list followed by an optional trailing field, storing the updated position.

name: write_pointer_list_entries
description: Walks a null-terminated list of pointers, writing a length word and the data for each entry through the file writer, then writes the optional trailing field. It returns one when all writes succeed.

name: free_icon_entry_list
description: Repeatedly takes the first entry from a linked list in the record and frees it through another routine until the list is empty.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so calling it performs no work.

name: call_helper_on_record_slot
description: Calls a routine with the same first argument and with the address of a fixed slot inside the record, then returns.

name: allocate_icon_node_record
description: Allocates a 168-byte node through the exec library, initialises its link field, passes it to another routine, and frees the node and returns zero if that routine fails; otherwise it returns the node.

name: call_helper_and_return
description: Calls one library routine and returns, with no other work.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Contains only a return of zero, so calling it has no effect beyond returning that value.

name: store_pair_in_slot_array
description: Stores a pair of values in the next free slot of a counted array held by the record. When no slot is free it first calls another routine to extend the array and returns zero if that fails; otherwise it returns one.

name: store_pair_in_free_slot
description: Takes the next free slot of the counted array, decrements the counter, stores the two given values in it, and returns one.

name: allocate_linked_icon_block
description: Allocates a 94-byte block through the exec library, links it through another routine, initialises its inner pointer fields and passes it to a second routine. It frees the block and returns zero when another routine fails; otherwise it returns the block.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so calling it performs no work.

name: release_block_return_zero
description: Releases a block through the exec library free routine and returns zero.

name: call_helper_on_record_slot
description: Calls a routine with the same first argument and with the address of a fixed slot inside the record, then returns.

name: find_tooltype_value
description: Walks a list of tool-type strings, comparing each entry with a key up to its equals sign, and returns the text after the equals sign for the first match or zero when none matches.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Contains only a return of zero, so calling it has no effect beyond returning that value.

name: search_pipe_separated_list
description: Scans a pipe-separated string list from a start position, comparing each segment's length and text with a key through another routine, and returns one when a matching segment is found or zero otherwise.

name: find_pipe_segment_match
description: Walks the pipe-separated segments of a string, checks each segment's length against the wanted length, and returns one when a segment's text also matches through another routine.

name: scan_pipe_segments_forward
description: Advances through pipe-separated segments of a string, checking each segment's length and matching its text through another routine, and returns one when a segment matches or zero when the string ends.

name: scan_pipe_segments_from_start
description: Restarts from the beginning of a pipe-separated string and checks each segment's length and text through another routine, returning one on a match or zero when no segment matches.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Contains only a return of zero, so calling it has no effect beyond returning that value.

name: parse_copy_prefix_name
description: Recognises a 'copy' or 'copy of' prefix in a name string, parses any decimal copy number that follows, and stores the remaining name text in the record.

name: parse_copy_count_from_name
description: Parses a decimal number that follows a copy prefix in the name; when the number is non-zero and the following text matches, it stores the number and the remaining text in the record.

name: parse_decimal_digits
description: Reads a run of decimal digits from the text and accumulates them into a number; when the number is non-zero and the next text matches a reference, it completes the parse.

name: parse_numbered_copy_format
description: Accumulates decimal digits from the current text position into a number, then checks the text that follows against the copy-number format reference and finishes the parse.

name: char_to_decimal_digit
description: Returns the numeric value of a character when it is an ASCII digit, or minus one for any other character.

name: call_alloc_mem_stub
description: Calls the exec memory allocation routine through the library base saved in global data and leaves its result in the return register.

name: obtain_register_or_release
description: Obtains a block from another routine and passes it to a second routine; when that second step fails it releases the block through a third routine and returns zero. Otherwise it returns the block.

name: allocate_icon_header_record
description: Allocates a 96-byte record through the exec library, sets its type field and a leading marker to ten, passes it to another routine that fills in the rest, and returns whether the allocation succeeded.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Contains only a return of zero, so calling it has no effect beyond returning that value.

name: check_library_result_matches
description: Calls a library routine with the given arguments and returns its count only when it equals the expected count; otherwise it returns zero.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so calling it performs no work.

name: check_library_result_matches
description: Calls a second library routine with the given arguments and returns its count only when it equals the expected count; otherwise it returns zero.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so calling it performs no work.

name: divide_unsigned_32bit
description: Performs unsigned 32-bit division by a 16-bit divisor and returns the quotient and remainder as a 64-bit pair, using a shift-and-subtract loop when the divisor is large.

name: divide_by_shift_subtract
description: Runs the bit-by-bit shift-and-subtract division loop on a 32-bit dividend, leaving the quotient and remainder in the working registers.

name: multiply_32bit_operands
description: Multiplies two 32-bit values using 16-bit partial products and returns the 64-bit result as a pair of 32-bit words.

name: call_rawdofmt_stub
description: Calls the exec formatting routine through the library base saved in global data, passing along the arguments it was given.

name: store_low_byte_at_pointer
description: Writes the low byte of the data register to the memory address held in the pointer register, storing one byte.

name: measure_string_length
description: Counts the characters of a null-terminated string and returns the count, not including the terminator.

name: find_char_in_string
description: Scans a null-terminated string for the given character and returns a pointer to its first occurrence, or zero when it is not present.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Contains only a return of zero, so calling it has no effect beyond returning that value.

name: copy_null_terminated_string
description: Copies a null-terminated string byte by byte, including its terminator, into the destination buffer.

name: append_string_to_end
description: Moves to the terminator of the destination string and copies the source string, including its terminator, after it.

name: compare_strings_up_to_count
description: Compares up to a given number of characters of two strings. It returns zero when they match through that count or through the end of the string, and one at the first mismatch.

name: stub_return_one
description: Contains only a return of one, so calling it has no effect beyond returning that value.

name: scan_string_with_limit
description: Walks through a string while the count stays positive and, at the terminator, calls a routine before returning.

name: call_helper_and_return
description: Calls one library routine and returns, with no other work.

name: copy_string_padded_to_length
description: Copies a null-terminated string into a fixed-length buffer, stopping at the given length, and fills any remaining bytes with zero.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so calling it performs no work.

name: initialise_exec_list_header
description: Sets up an empty exec-style list header: the head points at the tail slot, the tail is cleared, and the tail predecessor points back at the head.

name: read_optional_record_block
description: Returns one when no record is supplied; otherwise it reads a 20-byte block and then the nested data it points to, returning zero on failure.

name: process_linked_record_chain
description: Walks a linked chain of records, processing each 16-byte header and a sub-block whose size is four times a stored count, and follows the next-record pointer until the chain ends. Returns one on success and zero on failure.

name: stub_return_one
description: Contains only a return of one, so calling it has no effect beyond returning that value.

name: stub_return_zero
description: Contains only a return of zero, so calling it has no effect beyond returning that value.

name: read_icon_record_with_chunk
description: When a record is requested, allocates a cleared 20-byte record, reads its contents and a two-byte value, and stores that value in the record. It returns the record on success, minus one on failure, and zero when no record was requested.

name: stub_return_minus_one
description: Contains only a return of minus one, so calling it has no effect beyond returning that value.

name: read_record_chain_count
description: Reads a chain of 16-byte records, each followed by a sub-block whose size is four times a stored count, and links each record to the previous one. It returns the first record read, zero when none was requested, or minus one when a read fails.

name: read_record_list_head
description: Reads records one by one, linking each to the previous one and stopping when a record has no successor. It returns the last record read, or minus one when a read fails.

name: stub_empty_return
description: Contains only a return instruction, so calling it performs no work.

name: stub_return_minus_one
description: Contains only a return of minus one, so calling it has no effect beyond returning that value.

name: initialise_translator_library
description: Creates the library structure through the exec MakeLibrary routine, stores the caller's data and the base in it, and registers it with AddLibrary. It returns minus one on success and zero when the structure could not be made.
